instruction:
You have been tasked with designing a synchronous signal module in Verilog. The module should take in a clock signal (`clk`) and an input signal (`in`). The output should be a synchronized output signal (`out`), as well as synchronized falling (`falling`) and rising (`rising`) edge outputs.

The module should have a shift register that is three bits wide (`[2:0]`). On the rising edge of the clock signal, the shift register should shift its contents to the left by one bit, with the most significant bit (`[2]`) being discarded and the least significant bit (`[0]`) being replaced with the input signal (`in`).

The synchronized output signal (`out`) should be the middle bit of the shift register (`[1]`).

The synchronized falling edge output (`falling`) should be high when the most significant bit (`[2]`) is high and the middle bit (`[1]`) is low.

The synchronized rising edge output (`rising`) should be high when the most significant bit (`[2]`) is low and the middle bit (`[1]`) is high.

Write a Verilog module that implements the above specifications. Your module should be self-contained and should not require additional modules to function.
